_comment: Featured/curated Overton terms that bypass the podcast mention pipeline. These are pinned at the top of the Overton Window with a 'Debated' badge. Pipeline exports cannot overwrite this file.

featured.thesis: The money is not "debt is high." The switch is the rule that forces someone — banks, pensions, insurers — to own Treasury duration below a free clearing price. Post-WWII repression stuffed the system and crushed bondholders in real terms. Modern clothes: SLR / HTM / liquidity rules / possible backstops. If the franchise gets a spread and a put, bank equity can be a utility tollbooth. If it only gets stuffed, equity is the next boxcar. Debate who is forced to buy the paper and what they get paid — not deficit scare, not Nvidia.
featured.who_collects_rent: Whoever writes (and can rewrite) the captivity rule — regulators / Treasury / Fed plumbing — not the coupon.
featured.decisive_test: The next new 10-year and 30-year mid-month refunding print where (a) bid-to-cover softens hard, (b) primary-dealer accepted share jumps while indirect collapses, and (c) the stop-out tails worse than the last print's ~5–7bp through when-issued — dealers eat it and the captive does not show. Alternate test: announced SLR/Treasury-preference relief and bank aggregate Treasury holdings still fall for two reported quarters (rule without captivity).
featured.nested_note: Related but distinct thread (NOT a sibling card this week): power/interconnect as the AI switch (watts/queue), still not the chip.
featured.adjacent_note: Adjacent to but distinct from YCC — this card is about the captivity rule and who bears the paper, not the policy label.
